brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: Linear 3-cell base: piece:-1,0,0;half-n, piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, with capOpenFaces caps and lockJoints jointBolt
Two drop-in removable bins: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments) and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments)
drawer:0#-1,0#cut on the half-n base at (-1,0), set open to prove it clears; it faces outward with no neighbour in its pull direction
handle:0,0,0;top on cover:0,0,0;full;top in the centre cell, so the bins flank it

finish.summary: Built a portable electronics organizer: linear 3-cell base (half-n + 2 full), centre full base carries a top cover with a carry handle, flanking removable divided bins for small parts (div3 and div2), and a drawer in the end half base set open to show it works. Caps and joint locks applied; check_build ok, meshClash clear. Small-parts props staged earlier were removed because the checker flagged them under rim / blocking the drawer, so bins are shown empty.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
